label: text

Anti-British Agitators
Kept Out.

label: text
text: IMPROVEMENT AT CHUNGKING.

label: paragraph_title
text: Hankow Processions Diverted By Chinese Troops.

label: text
text:
There were large processions in Hankow yesterday (Sunday) but these were diverted by Chinese troops and were prevented from entering the Concession without difficulty. There was no disturbance of any kind.
H.M.S. "Cockechafers!" the s.s. "Wantung" and s.s.s. "Wanhsien" have arrived in Hankow.
They have come from up the five following the negotiations which followed the taking possession of the two B. and S. boats by General Yang Sen.

label: text
text: Chungking is, quieter. Supplies have been obtainable during the last two days and local officials have promised to afford protection. The outlook in Szechuan province is, however, uncertain at present.

label: text
text: Chungking is the last British trenty port up the Yangtse., in Szechuan province, and has suffered much as the result of intense feeling among the Chinese following the Wanhien incident, demonstrations having been held outside foreign residences, which were threatened, and hillside bungalows had to be hurriedly evacuated by foreign residents.

label: text
text: There have been a few cases of desultory firing at passing ships at Shasi and Hwangchow.—Naval Descatch.

label: text
text: [Shasi is further up than Hawkow and Hwangchow below. "Both ports are believed to be held by the southerners.]

label: text
text: The "Wanhsen, " arrived back in port a few days ago, Her Chief Officer Mr. Johnstone, and Chief Engineer Mr. Kerr went up to Kueifu for her and brought her down.

label: text
text: General Yang's Sen made use of her as he did of the "Th Ling" an American ship, and of three flying the French flag, to bring down what looks more like a horde of roughs than what they claim to be—soldiers. They were from Kuéifu and Wushan only.

label: text
text: The main army, following Yang Sen are said to be coming down from "Wanhsien," but just to-day news has come through that the troops favouring the south have started to attack Yang Sen, so they may be kept nearer home.

label: text
text: "The 'Wanhsien' shows much evidence of the attack made on her, and like, the 'Wantung' much sign of wanton destruction."

label: text
text: The British gunbouts "Mantis," "Teal" and "Widgeon" accompanied by the "Kiawo" have left for up river. A rise in the river made it possible for the larger of the gunbouts to go up. The "Bee," with Rear Admiral Cameron on board, the "Cricket," and the "Cockchafer" are still here. Mr. A. P. Slunt; the British Consul for Teang, has gone up river on the "Mantis" to continue the negotiations over the "Wanhsien" attack. There is much fear amongst the Chinese that, if Yang Sen arrives here with his army, he will go no farther.

label: text
text: The Chamber of Commerce has already raised $100,000; and now a similar sum is demanded.—N. C. Daily News.

label: paragraph_title
text: Slow Improvement.

label: paragraph_title
text: Shanghai, October

label: text
text: Conditions at ports on the upper Yangtse, recently swept by serious anti-British demonstrations which led to the evacuation of Chungking by the British community are reported to be slowly improving, according to reports received in Shanghai yesterday.

label: text
text: Anti-British agitation is reported to be still proceeding but no serious incident is reported.—“Shanghai Times.”

label: paragraph_title
text: And Then Worse?

label: paragraph_title
text: Peking, Oct. 11.

label: text
text: The position of the foreigners in Szechuan has become worse. A rigid anti-British boycott in Chungking and Wanhsen is being maintained by agitators who are striving to extend a similar boycott to Chengtu and elsewhere. Chinese are also threatening the missionaries at the mission stations in various cities in Szechuan, particularly in Chengtu—Reuter.

label: doc_title
text: CANTON'S MANIFESTO

label: doc_title
text: BOYCOTT SETTLED: BUT STRIKE NOT OVER!

label: paragraph_title
text: PRESENT KUOMINTANG POLICY DEFINED.

label: text
text:
Blockade of Hong Kong Given Up—Intensified Struggle Continues.
NATIONALIST GOVERNMENT SILENT: PICKET & COMMITTEE TO REMAIN.

label: text
text: A long official announcement by the Canton Government makes two statements of fact which are of the utmost importance from the point of view of “settlement of the boycott.” These are:—

label: text
text: A bureau of the government (the Canton Information Bureau) says categorically:—the Strike Committee called off the boycott.

label: text
text: In a declaration, the Strike Committee emphasises:—Therefore, we cannot say that the Canton and Hong Kong strike is settled.

label: text
text: The Nationalist Government has issued no proclamation.

label: text
text: The Kuomintang declaration lays stress on:—the giving up of the policy of direct boycott and the blockade of Hong Kong. But this same declaration, in a mass of political and other utterances, gives prominence to "intensification of the struggle against Imperialism." It is noteworthy that the Strikers specifically refer to Hong Kong and the Kuomintang does not.

label: text
text: Latest reports on the situation to-day appear below, revealing the effect of Sunday's decision.

label: paragraph_title
text: OFFICIAL MANIFESTO.

label: text
text: The following despatch has been sent by the Canton Information Bureau (a Government institution), via Reuter:—

label: text
text: "At a great gathering at the East Párade ground yesterday at noon the Strike Committee called off the boycott."

label: text
text: In this connection two Declarations have been issued:—one by the Strike Committee and the other by the Kuomintang addressed to the general body of Hong Kong and Canton strikers.

label: text
text: The Nationalist Government has issued no statement, the boycott being a patriotic popular movement under the leadership of the Strike Committee as the elected executive of the general body of the strikers.

label: text
text: The general sense of the Declarations is that though the specific struggle which has found expression in the boycott was directly caused by the Shanghai massacre of May 30 and the Shameen-Shakee massacre of June 23, the same is but a part of the general nationalist struggle against imperialism. Owing to fundamental change in the national situation brought about by an extension of Nationalist power and influence to the Yangtse, there is necessity to change the technique of the specific struggle and to resort to a new policy as well as to propaganda in order to make the people of the whole country realise the semi-colonial status of China and lead them to join the active anti-imperialist movement whose nim and purpose is the liberation of Nationalist China from unequal Treaties and the redress of wrongs.

label: text
text: After a review of the national revolutionary movement in China the Kuomintang Declaration to the strikers emphasises that "the giving up of the policy of direct boycott and the blockade of Hong Kong" (which is a specific struggle) does not mean the cessation of the general struggle of Chinese Nationalism against Imperialism but its intensification "on a national scale until the independence of China is completely secured." Argument is developed by comparing Kwangtung to "one" wing of a wide front and this one wing has advanced, very far while the rest of the front is not yet in a position for a similar advance.....Kwangtung.

label: text
text: Therefore, although successful in the anti-imperialist struggle is arresting its advance in order to concentrate its efforts in different directions in accordance with a new policy.

label: text
text: [Note: The above sentence is obviously mutilated in" transmission.]

label: text
text:
Victory, Not Defeat.
This policy which is now being
arried out with the same spirit of
self-discipline and self-sacrifice as
as the advance is not a defeat, but
great victory.

label: text
text: What is the new policy? Briefly, it means to consolidate the revolutionary base in Kwangtung, in other words, to consolidate the people's movement and make it a base for political and economic development, to improve local and provincial administration, to build ports and roads, to improve the living conditions of the workers, peasants, teachers, merchants, etc., to destroy banditry and make the political liberties of the people secure—all this means to make the national revolutionary base in Kwangtung so

label: text
text:
strong that no aggression by imperialists could affect us.
About the Future.

label: text
text: But this is not all. The new policy means a widening and strengthening of the National revolutionary base in other Provinces so that they can join in the active anti-imperialist front. The new policy means that much effort must be used in the re-establishment and strengthening of the people's organisations throughout the country and in securing revolutionary provincial and district government in the places which have already been occupied, or will be occupied in the future. When all this is done, then the anti-imperialist front will become unshakable and its final victory asquared. Then the independence and liberty of China and the welfare of the suffering masses will be secured.

label: text
text: In the "declarations of the Strike Committee after referring to the decision to "withdraw voluntarily all our pickets from various parts at 12 o'clock noon on October 10," they "solemnly declare to the public that we recognise the new policy as most suitable to our modern revolutionary environment and as the most

label: paragraph_title
text: CONDITIONS. FULFILLED.

label: text
text: On arrival of the China Navigation steamboat "Fatshan" here to-day, she "anchored in the stream.

label: text
text: Passengers went ashore and cargo was landed without interference.

label: text
text: All examiners (of the Strike organisation) have been withdrawn from boats plying between Canton and inland ports and cargo is now released. directly after examination by the Maritime Customs—" Wah Tsz. Yat Po."

label: text
text: effective measure for opposing imperialism. We make our resolution voluntarily; we have not arrived at any settlement with our enemy and, therefore, are under no obligation to him. We know only the needs of the National revolution and the need of the masses. This alone determines our policy and actions.

label: paragraph_title
text: Strike Not Settled.

label: text
text: "Our new policy does not mean that our anti-British responsibility ends to-day. Our Strike Committee and other strike organisations still exist. On the one hand, the Committee and the organisations will look for work for workmen who have sacrificed their all for the Strike for fifteen months. On the other hand, the Committee and organisations continue the general and specific struggle against imperialist atrocities together with different classes. Therefore, we cannot say that the Canton and Hong Kong strike is settled." In short, if the gunboat policy of the British is not changed, the massacres of May 30 and June 28 not redressed, our mission is not completed and the anti-British imperialist movement does not come to an end. Our duty is:

label: text
text: (a) To help with all our might the Northern Expedition to gain final victory and to secure victory for the people;

label: text
text:
(b) To resist imperialists without and to eradicate counter-revolutionaries within an order to make strong the Kwangtung revolutionary base;
(c) To assist in the reorganisation of the Provincial Government. To establish an

label: text
text: honest and efficient government in order to make the Government's policy coincide with its actions. We must have the people's interests protected and their freedom secured;

label: text
text:
"Domination of Hong Kong."
(d) To support the opening of the Whampoa Port and the extension of the Yueh-han (Canton-Hankow) Railway as well as the development of other industries so that Kwangtung will be delivered from the domination of Hong Kong. Then we will consolidate our position of economic independence and have full freedom of development;

label: text
text: (e): On the one hand, we shall strengthen our own forces; and on the other, we shall co-operate with all classes of the country to fight the barbarous policy of Imperialism and to secure the freedom and independence of China.

label: paragraph_title
text: MUCH IMPROVEMENT.

label: paragraph_title
text: Chinese Returning to Former Employers.

label: text
text: The boycott has been publicly announced at an and the Strike Committee have issued a proclamation to this effect.

label: text
text: Chinese are returning to duty with their former employers and the situation is much improved.

label: text
text: Arrangements are now being made for a general resumption of trade and business, but movements and berthing of steamboats are handicapped due to the sifting up of wharves during the strike.

label: text
text: Processions and demonstrations on Sunday, October 10, passed off peacefully.—Naval Despatch.

label: text
text: Strike pickets have been withdrawn but, pending the return of two delegates sent to Canton to ascertain the position. the boycott is being continued, and no employees of British are yet allowed to return.—Naval Despatch.

label: paragraph_title
text: CONDITIONS TO-DAY.

label: paragraph_title
text: River Steamers Resume Trips To Canton.

label: text
text: Hundreds of Chinese stood on the Praya this morning to see if it was true that communications had been resumed with Canton.

label: text
text: In addition to British shipping movements recorded below, the Tung On S.S. Co.'s "Sai On" left this morning.

label: text
text: There was no flourish of trumpets when the long-missed prodigal set off—after a year's exile on the Hong Kong-Macao run.

label: text
text: She carried between 200 and 300 passengers but no cargo. So soon as the "Tung On" comes out of dock, she will join her sister ship.

label: text
text: On inquiry from the management the “China Mail” was informed the “Sri On” would act on instructions from the British Consul General in Canton as to whether they should go alongside their own wharf or anchor in the stream.

label: text
text:
They had also heard that the river near the wharves had silted in the interval. (Note: This is confirmed by a despatch published by courtesy of the Naval authorities).
As yet no other "outside" boat has resumed the run. The "Kwong Tung's" owners wish to take up the night trip but are waiting for information as to the examination regulations—during the night—on account of martial law below Whampoa.

label: paragraph_title
text: WAR MYSTERY.

label: paragraph_title
text: Southerners Defeated Report.

label: text
text: KIUKIANG IN THE BALANCE

label: text
text: Struggle Being Extended to Two New Zones.

label: text
text: [By Our Special Correspondont.]

label: text
text: The fate of Kiukiang is in the balance.

label: text
text: Marshal Sun Chuan-fang claims to have repulsed each one of a series of southern drives on his main camp but the position is still obscure.

label: text
text: Details are given in latest despatches of small towns re-occupied by Allied troops who say that they have pushed the Cantonese away from the northern half of the railway between Kiukiang and Te-an.

label: text
text: Further inland from Te-an to Nanchang, less is known for want of communication.

label: text
text: The 7th Canton Army appears to have been used as "shock troops in the offensive of Kiukiang and is being replaced by the two famous divisions from the 4th Army.

label: paragraph_title
text: Allies on Defence.

label: text
text: Indications are that the south-erners have not lost their grip on the situation and that Sun Chuanfang is still concentrating on defence of his base at Kiukiang.

label: text
text: On the Fukien-Kwangtung frontier, the opposing troops are in the field but fighting is only on a small scale.

label: text
text: Chinese reports state that General Yang Sen is still anti-Canton and that he is marching victoriously eastwards to attack the southern bases (on their line of communication) between Yochow and Changsha.

label: text
text: Another report which hints at the war spreading to another new zone is that "from " Canton, with reference to possible developments in or near Kwangsi.

label: text
text: General Wong Shiu-hung, governor of Kwangsi province (with headquarters at Wuchow) has called a report to the Nationalist Government that Yunnanese troops are threatening Kwangsi but have not entered the province.

label: text
text: Gen. Fan Shek-sang (pro-Nationalist mercenary leader) has proceeded to Pak-sik.—Wah Tsz Yat Po.

label: text
text:
Swatow, Oct. 11.
It is reported that the local (Cantone) troops are being drawn back from the (adjoining) Fukien border.—Naval Despatch.

label: paragraph_title
text: KIUKIANG COMPLEX.

label: text
text: Definite Statement That Town is Quiet.

label: text
text:
Hankow, Oct. 11.
All is quiet at Klukiang.--Navu.
Despatch.

label: text
text: Though various rumours have been in circulation for the past few days as to the situation at Kiukiang, the situation remains unchanged, according to a Kiukiang message received by the Japanese Navy this morning.—Toho.

label: text
text: Out of the 18th Brigade under the command of General Feng Shao-ming which are now stationed at Hsluchien, about 2,000 soldiers arrived at Pukow, the opposite side of Hsluchien yesterday and proceeded to Klukiang this afternoon by the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Company's stepmers—Toho.

label: paragraph_title
text:
Talk, Then a Halt.
Klukiang, Oct. 4.

label: text
text: The much talked of western advance by huge forces of Sun Chuan-fang's troops through the province of Kiangsi has come to a sudden halt.

label: text
text: A slight distance outside of Nanchang, towards the west of the city, they met with the crack troops of General Chang Kai-shek, and were badly defeated. Sun's forces are now being driven back toward Nanchang.

label: text
text: Authentic reports have been received to the effect that the Revolutionary forces are concentrating south of Nanchang for the purpose of making a big drive against Sun Chuan-fang's troops at Nanchang and Kluikang
